the test-case sequence that proves it, and the outcomes expected at each
significant step. It is the layer that makes operational meaning

A testing frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation executes

concepts.definition: Four distinct claims: contract sufficiency asks whether every participant can determine and perform its responsibility from declared interfaces/context; boundary congruence asks whether actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority; path realisation asks whether the exact runnable subject uses the authoritative entry-to-outcome path; user usability asks whether the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtains the outcome using only declared context, access and supported surfaces.

grounding.quote:

| boundary congruence | Do the actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve the declared domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority? An actual-composition claim acquires both sides and their exchanges; design correspondence alone proves no implementation behaviour. |
| path realisation | Does the exact runnable subject use the authoritative entry-to-outcome path through its material state, effect and observation boundaries? Matching output through another path is insufficient. |
| user usability | Can the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtain the selected outcome using only its declared context, access and supported surface? Internal success or validator-aware fixtures cannot establish this claim. |

and cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer (P6). The two

carry assertion provenance from the first chain and executions carry

Every designed module, function, application surface, runtime surface,

concepts.definition: Subject-described Tier 1 STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, a_c: domain-specific and carrier-neutral, with stable identity urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c in urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus. Its member owns position/scope, signature, record shapes, AC-001–AC-020, traversals/functor kinds, interpretation/models, three layers, calculus identity, application/import/exclusion boundaries and conformance obligations. It consumes FOUNDATIONS ontology and core results without redefining them; clauses identify their requiring P0–P6 principles. Its definitions do not depend on derivation-record layout, selected interpretation, carrier, provider, runtime or repository topology.

grounding.quote:
Tier 1. Owns the a_c theory in full: position and scope, the signature,
the typed records, the laws AC-001 to AC-020, traversals and functor
kinds, interpretation and models, the three governed layers, the law of
calculus identity, the application boundary, external imports, exclusions
and the conformance obligations of this member. Consumes the ontology of
[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md) (subject, representation, interpretation,
context, object, claim, evidence, judgment, authority, residual, basis,
material) and the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); it states laws over
those objects and defines none of them a second time. Each clause names
the principle (P0 to P6) that requires it, as
[FOUNDATIONS §1](FOUNDATIONS.md#1-vocabulary-of-standing) requires.

The STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, written `a_c`,
is this method's domain-specific, carrier-neutral constitutional calculus
for representing and relating governed symbolic systems. Its stable
concept identity is `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c`. This member
owns that concept in the bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus`. Both identifiers are
declared identities and do not change with the carrier or the directory
that publishes them (P3).

governed layers with separate content identities and proof boundaries
(§7). A layer becomes a released Product only through separately

The calculus specialises the governing commitments declared in this

concepts.definition: Material family F9's premise-to-rule account distinguishes derived consequences from owner-selected choices. Instance premises, not supplied by commitments, are: a finite model represents governed objects/relations/constraints/residuals/traversals/transformations/judgments; exact subject, interpreted model and possible carrier have separate identities; some predicates are mechanical and others need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication. P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are marked independent; P0 recovered; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6. Nineteen rows bind these premises to position, scope, signature, identity/typing, authority/basis, results, latitude, residuals, closure/projection, overlay, transformation, judgment separation, traversal/composition, interpretation, layers, identity issuance, application/import boundaries, constraint surfaces and qualification.

grounding.quote:
This member is material family F9, the `a_c` calculus. The table below
shows which of its rules follow from which premises, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
which also states the standing of the consequences. Instance premises,
which the commitments do not supply:

- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose
  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,
  traversals, transformations and judgments;
- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in
  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;
- (iii) some predicates over a model are decided mechanically, and others
  need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication.

concepts.definition: M_b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J), with exact basis b, closed identity universe I and finite populations for semantic objects, directed relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations and judgments. Population_M is total over the eight core kinds. Local_M is their disjoint union; I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M. RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind, field) yields cardinality, allowed local kinds, semantic-object sorts, external target kinds and required basis relation.

grounding.quote:
`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population
is finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and
record identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be
that union. Then `I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M`, where every
member of `External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared
external reference domain and exact resolution relation. A hidden record,
an unpopulated extra record family, an identity occurring in two
populations, or an identity in `I` with neither one local record nor one
lawful external resolution refuses the model. A population may be empty
only when the selected signature does not require a member of that record
kind (P3, P5).

external reference relation, not a ninth fundamental record family. Every
field is identity-bearing and exact. One external identity has exactly one
resolution tuple in one model; a missing, ambiguous or extra tuple refuses
(P3).

concepts.label: External resolution coordinate and preservation witness

concepts.label: Subject Judgment record

conditions: A requirement claims meaningful system behaviour.

grounding.quote:
Features are not proved by isolated assertions alone. Where a requirement
claims meaningful system behaviour, the proving surface should be a scenario
bundle or an equivalent ordered set of test cases that exercises that
behaviour through a coherent sequence rather than as disconnected
fragments (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Isolated assertions alone do not prove features. The proving surface should use a scenario bundle or equivalent ordered cases exercising coherent behaviour. Scenarios and use cases force operational intent/design to expose boundaries, sequences, actors, controls and outcomes; the significant paths they identify must be exercised.

conditions: The system has an installable or runnable development form.

grounding.quote:
proof should prefer a fresh sandbox or equivalent isolated environment, an
installed or built development artifact, and execution through the same
declared entry, control and runtime surfaces the real product uses. Direct
source-level or unit-level checks may stay useful; they do not replace
installed-dev proof of the system under test (P6; SPEC_METHOD §6 for the
install and development-product roles).

constraints.statement: The decisive lane runs against an installed development target, not solely the source tree. It should prefer fresh isolation, an installed/built artifact and the Product's declared entry/control/runtime surfaces. Useful source/unit checks do not replace this proof.

grounding.quote:
If the significant paths are not declared, scenario coverage cannot be
judged. If they are declared and not exercised, the behaviour is not fully
proved (P6; EVALUATION §1, a claim's scope cannot exceed its evaluated
evidence).

constraints.statement: The proving surface declares and exercises meaningful paths intentionally; exhaustive proof does not require every possible branch in every file. Undeclared paths make scenario coverage unjudgeable; declared but unexercised significant paths leave behaviour not fully proved. Claim scope cannot exceed evaluated evidence. The listed path classes are usual and relevance-dependent, not a universal exhaustive checklist.

grounding.quote:
Producing an expected output through a bypass, an obsolete executor, a
test-only seam, an undeclared fallback or a competing authority falsifies
path conformance even when the output value is equal (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Files, suites, runners, fixtures, scenario labels, coverage percentages and actors do not become frames merely by existing. Authority stays within the exercised claim; counts, source coverage, duration and framework category do not enlarge it. Equal output through bypass, obsolete executor, test-only seam, undeclared fallback or competing authority falsifies path conformance. Cross-participant combinations cannot be mocked away and counted as unit evidence.

conditions: Testing frames have been selected under governing configuration or admitted work authority.

grounding.quote:
The fan-out assigns claims to evidence; it is neither an authority
hierarchy nor a claim that one frame decomposes into another. Evidence
may relate through declared conjunction
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),
translation (REFERENCE_FRAME §6), falsification and re-entry (P4a). A
broader frame cannot make a module-owned
law true, and any number of narrower green frames cannot establish an
unevaluated Product composition or user outcome (EVALUATION §1, the weaker
property never substitutes for the claimed one).

constraints.statement: Frame selection is determined by evaluated claim, subject, path, population, oracle and falsification boundary, not runner kind. The four frames introduce no role, stage, authority or hierarchy and do not decompose into one another. Each claim is assigned congruent evidence: user outcome to UAT, runnable causal path to end to end, composition boundary to integration, module law to unit. Internal complexity sets unit evidence size/strategy, never eligibility. Broader evidence cannot make a module law true; arbitrarily many narrower successes cannot establish an unevaluated Product composition/outcome. Frame labels without declarations have no assurance value. Each core result retains its claim predicate; invalidation rows only instantiate material-input or basis changes under ACTIVATION §7, adding no other invalidator.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced activation, frame-declaration and core-result owners are not supplied in full.

grounding.quote:
| exclusions | source imports, private APIs, direct Product-state injection, test-only endpoints, hidden administrator capability, undeclared fixtures or substitutes, a test double at a boundary claimed as real or live, compatibility bypasses, and internal success substituted for the user outcome |
| result | one core result bound to the exact user-outcome claim, with witnessed paths, counterexamples, residual user populations and invalidation conditions |
| invalidation | a material change of Product, supported interface, user role, capability, configuration, dependency or substitution mode, data contract, runnable subject, acceptance meaning or ordinary path |

constraints.statement: UAT obeys applicable Product/requirement outcomes, supported-interface, identity, UX, safety, persistence and release law, RF-001–017 and EVALUATION §§1,2,3,6,7. It has bounded evaluation authority only: no new Product meaning or acceptance ownership. Exclude source imports, private APIs, state injection, test-only endpoints, hidden administrator power, undeclared fixtures/substitutes, doubles at claimed real/live boundaries, compatibility bypasses and internal success substituted for user outcome. Return one exact-claim core result with witnessed paths, counterexamples, residual users and invalidators. Material changes to Product, interface, role, capability, configuration, dependency/substitution mode, data contract, runnable subject, acceptance meaning or ordinary path invalidate it.

conditions: Harnessed sandbox UAT is admitted, or a claim depends on real external compute or transport.

grounding.quote:
Where harnessed sandbox UAT is admitted (§2), a deterministic, fake,
recorded or injected external worker or transport limits the result to the
composed Product relations actually exercised; it does not prove that the
live external boundary works. When a Product or release claim depends on
real external compute or transport, live sandbox UAT is mandatory for that
claim; unit, integration, semantic and end-to-end evidence that uses the
substitute, and harnessed UAT green, are not sufficient (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Deterministic, fake, recorded or injected workers/transports restrict harnessed UAT results to exercised composed relations and prove no live boundary. A Product/release claim depending on real external compute/transport requires live sandbox UAT for that claim; substitute-based unit, integration, semantic, end-to-end evidence and harnessed UAT success are insufficient.
constraints.uncertainty: Section 2's admission conditions are outside the supplied source.

grounding.quote:
| exclusions | source-only substitutes for runnable-Product claims, direct invocation below the supported entry, test doubles at claimed real boundaries, test-only routing, hidden retries or repair, omitted persistence or fresh-process boundaries, and equal output without path evidence |
| result | one core result bound to the exact end-to-end claim, with the exercised composition edges, unexercised material paths, counterexamples and residual combinations |
| invalidation | a material change of artifact, install, dependency, configuration, interface, owner, path, lifecycle, persistence, recovery, projection, test semantics or evidence population |

constraints.statement: Governed by Product/accepted-design composition, exact-subject/assurance congruence, path singularity where required and lifecycle, authority, persistence, replay, recovery and release law. Observation may expose internals but cannot bypass, repair, replace or reinterpret the path. Exclude source-only runnable substitutes, below-entry calls, doubles at real boundaries, test routing, hidden retry/repair, omitted persistence/fresh-process boundaries and output without path evidence. Return an exact-claim core result with exercised edges, unexercised material paths, counterexamples and residual combinations. Material artifact/install/dependency/configuration/interface/owner/path/lifecycle/persistence/recovery/projection/test-semantics/evidence-population changes invalidate it. Expected output is necessary but insufficient; forbidden or obsolete paths falsify the claim. One process, many lines or an end-to-end label do not establish frame identity.

grounding.quote:
| exclusions | mocks or stubs that hide the claimed real contract, one-sided contract assertions, happy-path-only exchange, helper-call equivalence, flattened versions or states, and projection of a boundary result to the whole Product without a governing relation |
| result | one core result for the declared integration claim, with covered combinations, counterexamples, omitted interactions and invalidation conditions |
| invalidation | a material change of participant, interface, carrier, state, configuration, dependency, timing, failure, recovery or interaction population |

constraints.statement: Apply declared interface/composition law, complete participant admission, applicable atomicity/reconstruction and exact assurance boundaries. Boundary evaluation neither establishes an unevaluated Product outcome nor authorises substitution. Exclude mocks hiding real contracts, one-sided assertions, happy-path-only exchanges, helper equivalence, flattened versions/states and whole-Product projection without a governing relation. Return one integration core result with covered combinations, counterexamples, omissions and invalidators. Material participant/interface/carrier/state/configuration/dependency/timing/failure/recovery/population changes invalidate it.

grounding.quote: | authority | bounded local evidence only; a unit result has no Product, installed, integration, user-acceptance, architecture, path-selection or release authority |

No Product, user-outcome, installed-path, cross-module composition or
release claim may be closed from unit evidence, whatever the test count,
assertion count, source coverage, mutation score, runtime or historical
pass rate. Treating unit green as broader assurance is a frame error (P6,
EVALUATION §1).

constraints.statement: Unit proof obeys DESIGN_MODULE ownership/proof law and accepted ontology, carriers, domain, sequence, state, algorithm and error relations. It excludes Product outcomes, cross-module composition, supported user paths, packaging/install, real external participants, orchestration topology, mocked-away interface behaviour, incidental branches/private layout, assertion counts and source coverage as broader assurance. Return one exact-law/module-population core result with counterexamples, residual combinations and invalidators. Material changes to ontology, carriers, boundary, law, algorithm, state space, numerical regime, implementation, oracle, generator or bounded population invalidate it. No unit metric or success closes Product, user, installed, composition or release claims or supplies architecture/path-selection authority.

conditions: A module has code.

grounding.quote:
This frame does not waive the module-derived unit lane. It binds the lane
to module-owned law and the smallest congruent evidence population. Low
internal combinatorial complexity justifies a small lane, not omission and
not hundreds of implementation-shaped tests. Unit-test volume has no
independent closure value (P2).

constraints.statement: Every coded module requires the design-owned module-derived unit lane; public contracts are eligible. Complexity determines proportional size/strategy and the smallest congruent population, not omission or large implementation-shaped suites. Independent oracles often discriminate algebras, calculations, transformations, parsers, reducers, state machines, decision tables, admission/conservation relations and bounded algorithms especially well. Repeating implementation or incidental branches yields weak/circular evidence. Predominantly composition, orchestration, configuration, persistence, ownership or user-interaction complexity needs evidence at its actual integration/end-to-end/UAT boundary; mocking it does not create unit evidence.

grounding.quote:
The activated frame declares the finite interaction population and why its
covering set is adequate. Pairwise or other covering-array reduction is
lawful only where the basis explains why the omitted higher-order
interactions cannot change the claim, or keeps them as residuals.
High-consequence authority, persistence, concurrency, recovery, migration
and historically failure-prone relations normally need explicit
higher-strength combinations (P5, P2; REFERENCE_FRAME §8, interaction and
failure coverage).

constraints.statement: Activated frames declare finite interaction populations and covering-set adequacy. Unit dimensions remain module-bounded; value normally rises with closed-domain internal complexity. Integration/end-to-end/UAT value can be multiplicative through composed pre/postconditions, authority, state, configuration, failure and recovery, but depends on interactions actually discriminated, not sunny-path interface count. Common Product factors include user role/capability, operation/composition, definition/owner/implementation/dependency, lifecycle/persisted state, configuration/version, process/continuation/retry/re-entry/recovery, success/refusal/malformed/partial-failure/rival cases, fresh process/replay/reconstruction/migration and visible outcome/projection. High-consequence authority, persistence, concurrency, recovery, migration and historically fragile relations normally need explicit higher-strength coverage. Code visitation metrics do not establish semantic combinations, authoritative selection, user coverage or rival-path absence.

conditions: A Product path claim is made.

grounding.quote:
Every Product path claim needs two-sided evidence (P6, P3):

1. required-path reachability: each required authoritative composition has
   an exact witness in the deployed, installed or otherwise runnable
   Product form through the supported ordinary path; and
2. forbidden-path exclusion: each material superseded, duplicate,
   fallback, bypass or otherwise forbidden production path is absent,
   unreachable or refused at its declared boundary.

constraints.statement: Every required authoritative composition needs an exact supported ordinary-path witness in the runnable Product. Every material superseded, duplicate, fallback, bypass or other forbidden production path must be absent, unreachable or refused at its declared boundary. Successor success proves no predecessor removal. No obsolete/bypass/fallback/rival path may remain reachable in scoped production closure; no obsolete assurance consumer may falsely prove closure or reintroduce removed production paths. A forbidden-path outcome falsifies the path claim.

conditions: Path-sensitive mutation or sabotage is proportionate and safe.

grounding.quote:
A Product outcome reached through a forbidden path is a falsified path
claim, not a passing Product test. A negative-path test that mutates the
exact subject without isolation, restoration and subject revalidation
invalidates its own assurance basis (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Assurance includes checks that disabling the authoritative path prevents scenario success, restoring a rival produces refusal/detected counterexample, corrupting material interface/owner output is detected at its owning boundary, and removing an asserted obsolete path preserves accepted outcome except through the declared deletion relation. Negative tests mutating the exact subject without isolation, restoration and subject revalidation invalidate their own basis.

grounding.quote:
Each bound result states which
predicate it establishes; a result over a necessary condition does not
establish the obligation, and the sufficiency of a conjunction is a claim
of its own ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation))
(P6).

constraints.statement: A shared execution can yield distinct UAT outcome, end-to-end path, integration seam evidence and module-algebra counterexamples. Claims combine only through declared REFERENCE_FRAME §6 relations and FOUNDATIONS conjunction, with each predicate retained. Necessary-condition evidence does not establish the obligation; conjunction sufficiency is a separate claim. Default responsibilities remain user outcome, complete authoritative runnable path, material participant composition and proportionate module-law evidence respectively. UAT alone may leave path singularity open; end-to-end alone may leave user populations/combinations open; integration/unit cannot substitute for either. When all are required, conflicts and missing results remain visible to the decision owner and cannot be hidden by aggregate success.
constraints.uncertainty: The imported conjunction law is referenced but not supplied in full.

conditions: The assessed claim depends on owner-issued truth.

grounding.quote:
Where the acquired observation cannot
separate two admissible subjects on which the assessed predicate takes
opposite truth values, the frame returns further evidence, a justified
narrower scope or `indeterminate`. The binding of the
observation itself needs support
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation),
Observation sufficiency) (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Harnesses, fixtures, expected-value builders, proof scripts, evaluators and assessors cannot reconstruct parallel owner state from raw payloads/events/logs/filenames/labels/implementation fragments and treat it as the Product. Observation bindings require support. If admissible subjects with opposite predicate truth remain observationally indistinguishable, seek further evidence, justify narrower scope or return indeterminate. The semantic oracle derives independently from Product, requirement and accepted design, not mandatory trust in implementation. Missing owner projections/observable seams remain named assurance/design gaps; harnesses cannot fill them with rival semantics.

grounding.quote:
One unique violated locus and a jointly established set
map to `satisfied`. Unresolved alternative frontiers map to
`indeterminate`, naming the alternatives that further evidence must
decide between. The fourth form is the core value `indeterminate` itself,
naming the evidence a bounded frontier needs. The form travels with the
value as the domain outcome, so a joint set stays distinct from a unique
locus and unresolved alternatives stay distinct from an unbounded
frontier. Purpose and material relation: a localisation combines with
other results in the one core, and an unresolved causal explanation is
never read as an established one (P5, P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Exactly one frontier form is returned. Unique locus and jointly established minimal incomparable loci map to satisfied for the predicate that evidence establishes earliest violated loci; unresolved alternatives map to indeterminate naming alternatives, and unbounded frontier maps to indeterminate naming needed evidence. Preserve the domain form alongside the core value. Record subject, basis, frontier form/members, causal evidence, expected relations, observed counterexample and invalidated downstream claims. Do not choose an arbitrary owner from joint causes or convert alternatives into joint causes. Localisation grants no broader tests, compatibility repair, controller or upstream reinterpretation; scope/design change follows existing re-entry.

conditions: The composite refinement is activated.

grounding.quote:
| result and relations | each activated claim returns a core result with its exact evidence, coverage, causal findings and residuals; shared evidence is referenced once; mandatory claims compose only through a declared same-basis or lawful-translation conjunction (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results) to the named decision consumer |
| invalidation | a material change of contract, domain, participant, prompt or context, capability, callable path, configuration, translation, relevant workspace observation, lifecycle, oracle or evidence population invalidates the affected conclusions; unchanged valid evidence and owner rulings stay reusable |
| qualification | the representative sensitivity and refusal cases below, bound to actual subjects, actor envelopes and independently stated expected relations; mechanical source checks supply no semantic or live-user qualification |

constraints.statement: Apply selected Product/requirement/design/interface law, REFERENCE_FRAME declaration/translation law, FOUNDATIONS conjunction and existing testing-owner law. Equal shape/output implies no equal meaning, provenance or authority. Owners retain semantic, operation, admission and reserved decisions; bounded evaluation grants construction only under an existing exact operation grant and returns closed results to the declared decision consumer. Evidence binds contracts/both sides, design relations plus unresolved realisation facts for design claims, or actual requests/context/responses, callables/configuration, owner validation, effects/observations and ordinary-caller outcomes for realised claims, with independent expectations and substitution limits. Access must not alter reviewed subjects; required independence is claim-relative. Exclude hidden context/privilege, rival contract truth, inferred authority, undeclared substitutes, private/test paths for ordinary claims, candidate-as-admission, fixture-as-user evidence and unsupported whole-Product/future claims. Each activated claim returns exact evidence, coverage, causal findings and residuals; shared evidence is referenced once and mandatory claims compose only through declared same-basis/lawful-translation conjunction. Material contract/domain/participant/prompt/context/capability/path/configuration/translation/workspace/lifecycle/oracle/population changes invalidate affected conclusions; unchanged valid evidence/rulings remain reusable. Mechanical source checks give no semantic or live-user qualification.

grounding.quote:
The activation selects claims from the work's applicability (ACTIVATION §1)
and states the scope reason for each unselected claim; an unselected claim
has no result. Design-only work
does not require unavailable runtime evidence and does not report runtime or
UAT satisfaction. An unknown material condition keeps its dependent claim
unresolved: the claim's result is never `satisfied` and names the
condition as what would decide it
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing); omission
cannot close it. A full end-to-end usability claim
needs all four distinct results and their explicit conjunction
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),
in which an unselected claim is uncovered coverage. Transport,
parse, admission, semantic satisfaction, operation completion and user
success are not interchangeable (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Activation selects applicable claims and records scope reasons for every unselected claim, which has no result. Design-only work can establish contract sufficiency without runtime, keeps realisability/context uncertainty explicit, requires no unavailable runtime evidence and claims no runtime/UAT satisfaction. Actual-composition claims acquire both sides/exchanges; design correspondence proves no implementation behaviour. Matching output on another path does not prove path realisation; internal or validator-aware fixture success does not prove usability. Unknown material conditions leave dependent claims unresolved, never satisfied, naming deciding conditions; omission does not close them. Full end-to-end usability requires four distinct results plus explicit conjunction; an unselected claim is uncovered. Transport, parse, admission, semantic satisfaction, operation completion and user success remain distinct.

conditions: For every material seam.

grounding.quote:
1. Bind the functional input domain, producer success postconditions,
   consumer preconditions, permitted effects, refusals and observable exit.
   Direct successful handoff requires the producer's guarantees to meet the
   consumer's preconditions. An interface may instead emit candidates:
   candidate output, later admission and semantic assessment stay distinct
   declared stages. A normal model refusal or an inadmissible candidate does
   not by itself falsify an adequately declared candidate interface; the
   exact promised outcome and refusal behaviour are evaluated (P4a, P5).

constraints.statement: Reuse existing truth surfaces; add only missing cross-interface relations, without making schemas/prompts/adapters/indexes/tests contract owners. Bind functional inputs, producer success guarantees, consumer preconditions, effects, refusals and exit; direct success requires guarantees to meet preconditions. Candidate output, admission and semantic assessment remain declared distinct stages; normal refusal/inadmissible candidates alone do not falsify an adequate candidate contract. Supply material actor obligations/domains through actual context/interface or an exactly locatable lawfully resolvable source. Bind material LLM role, instructions, context, tools and model/transport configuration. Generic governance access neither supplies Product-specific contracts nor authorises hidden-rule inference. Deterministic owners expose computed facts by reuse/proven equivalent projection; semantic actors judge meaning within that domain, without inferring reserved rulings, eligibility, authority or admission from responses/labels.

conditions: For every material seam and each later operation on a mutable workspace.

grounding.quote:
4. Observe the relevant current mutable workspace for each later
   operation, and bind that observation separately from immutable
   authority, artifacts, history and prior candidates. Changed support
   invalidates dependent conclusions; unaffected accepted work stays
   reusable. A snapshot does not replace the current subject, and a change
   of actor alone is no reason to repeat still-valid work (P3, P4b;
   ACTIVATION §7).

constraints.statement: Preserve domain/time meaning through serialisation, parsing, normalisation and adaptation. Translation binds source/target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, governing owner and refusal conditions. Distinguish proposed/admitted/assessed/completed, active input/history and current validity/available bytes; equal wire shape proves no translation. Bind current workspace observations separately from immutable authority, artifacts, history and candidates; changed support invalidates dependencies while unaffected accepted work remains reusable. Snapshots cannot replace current subjects; actor changes alone do not justify repeating valid work. Follow actual callable paths/effect owners through selected exit and required fresh observation; hidden fallback, injection, repaired output, private entry or undeclared retry cannot support ordinary-path claims. Evaluation gives pure functions no new event lifecycle.

grounding.quote:
6. Preserve diagnostic cause through wrappers and projections. Apply §12:
   report the supported causal frontier, not merely the first log or clock
   occurrence. Keep the originating seam, bounded field or path, expected
   domain or basis, observed mismatch and evidence locator where available,
   with downstream symptoms, successful work and the declared continuation
   or block. Preserve joint causes, alternative frontiers and
   indeterminacy; do not invent a unique cause. Product redaction rules
   still govern sensitive content. Missing required diagnostic evidence
   stays a named gap. Return the smallest supported owner or re-entry;
   diagnosis grants no repair or retry (P5, P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: Preserve supported causal frontier through wrappers/projections, including available originating seam, bounded field/path, expected domain/basis, mismatch and evidence locator, downstream symptoms, successful work and declared continuation/block. Retain joint causes, alternatives and indeterminacy; invent no unique cause. Product redaction still applies; missing diagnostics remain named gaps. Return the smallest supported owner/re-entry; diagnosis authorises no repair/retry. Acquire facts from existing owner surfaces and use independent contract-derived oracles. Computed facts, contextual judgments and reserved owner rulings retain separate owners and validity scopes.

conditions: An LLM-interface usability claim is selected.

grounding.quote:
For an LLM-interface usability claim, clean-room LLM UAT is used, with the
ordinary supplied context and permitted tools and without private
implementation knowledge or fixture assistance. Expected outcomes are
recorded before responses are inspected. The sunny case and the ordinary
ambiguity and negative cases material to the claim are included.
Substitutes are disclosed; replayed or fabricated responses prove only
their stated narrower relation, not live-provider usability. Responses are
not edited, and nothing is silently retried until green. Live claims need
live evidence under §2, not a new universal live-provider requirement
during design (P6, P5; EVALUATION §3, expectations before exposure).

constraints.statement: Use clean-room LLM UAT with ordinary context/permitted tools and no private implementation knowledge or fixture help. Record expectations before inspecting responses and include material sunny, ordinary ambiguity and negative cases. Disclose substitutes; replay/fabrication proves only declared narrower relations. Do not edit responses or silently retry to success. Live claims require live evidence under §2; this is no universal live-provider requirement during design.

grounding.quote:
An early sunny thread can establish bounded evidence while the unexercised
claims stay open (the sequencing heuristic of SPEC_METHOD §8). This frame
adds no exhaustive-hardening prerequisite, scenario quota, controller,
runtime, generator, routine human approval, new ledger or automatic extra
agent. Existing authority selects proportionate assurance and any further
operation. The result returns, for each of the four claims, its core
result or the scope reason it was not selected, the exact
exercised subject and path, the supported mismatch, retained work,
substitutions, residuals and invalidators in the existing work carrier; it
is neither acceptance nor a grant of the next action (P2, P6; ACTIVATION
§6).

constraints.statement: Early sunny evidence can be bounded while unexercised claims remain open. The frame creates no exhaustive-hardening prerequisite, quota, controller, runtime, generator, routine human approval, ledger or automatic agent. Existing authority chooses proportionate assurance/further operations. Existing work carriers retain each of four claim results or nonselection reasons, exact subject/path, supported mismatch, retained work, substitutions, residuals and invalidators. This return is neither acceptance nor permission for the next action.

conditions: Material computational composition or recurrence work.

grounding.quote:
An identifiable complete-path result and its evidence return to the
declared decision consumer; a collection of local successes cannot replace
that result. Design-only evidence establishes only the design claim; claims
about actual work need observations on the selected path. Valid unchanged
results are reused, and affected reassessment is activated on a material
change of path, basis or workload. This is a bounded composition of
existing frames, not a permanent actor, an extra frame family, a per-helper
review or a separate accounting ledger (P4b, P2).

constraints.statement: Qualification challenges declared workload/operational assumptions while preserving independent scope, freshness and effect checks serving distinct obligations. Return an identifiable complete-path result/evidence to the decision consumer; local successes cannot replace it. Design evidence establishes only design claims; actual work needs selected-path observations. Reuse unchanged valid results and activate affected reassessment for material path/basis/workload changes. No permanent actor, new frame family, per-helper review or separate ledger is created.

conditions: A representative qualification case is selected.

grounding.quote:
These are representative source-contract discriminators: not an executed
trial, a universal test quota or whole-Product qualification. Each selected
case binds its own exact subject, oracle, evidence and claim scope (P6,
P5; EVALUATION §7).

constraints.statement: Cases are representative source-contract discriminators, not executed trials, quotas or whole-Product qualification; each binds exact subject/oracle/evidence/scope. Discriminate: ordinary usability of empty and nonempty eligible domains, with hidden required rules defeating sufficiency despite correct refusal; legitimate candidate refusal/filtering versus inadequate interfaces or violated success guarantees, with variability alone not failure; owner-defined eligibility/lifecycle versus available/equal-looking historical or same-response references; temporal/admission mismatch despite valid matching shapes; lost units/default/identity/order despite validation; hidden-rule fixture success versus unproved ordinary usability; forbidden-path equal output as falsified realisation; refresh affected workspace evidence while keeping unaffected valid work; retain originating causal frontier/uncertainty rather than symptoms or invented causes; design-only contract closure without inferred runtime/UAT satisfaction.

conditions: A new or materially changed realisation boundary is governed by a design profile.
exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor cites the accepted relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta without recreating evidence.

grounding.quote:
When the
design's co-evolution condition holds, the two chains may proceed together
without making implementation semantic authority; design still owns the
structural HOW. Where the design is not decision-complete, the relation is
design-gated at the smallest causally closed affected decision set and
retained implementation follows its acceptance. An unchanged
`realization_refactor` (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes) cites the accepted
relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not
recreate the evidence (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Evidence feedback cannot select/accept semantic answers. Assertion and execution provenance remain separate; agreement may share error and disagreement requires diagnosis. When the design's co-evolution condition holds, chains may proceed together without implementation semantic authority; design owns structural HOW. Incomplete design gates retained implementation at acceptance of the smallest causally closed affected decision set. For probabilistic/agentic construction, ACTIVATION §1 owns accepted-design handoff into bounded construction, assessment, disposition, checkpoint and continuation; the profile supplies governing-frame, transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction, computational-realisation and module evidence, not a second protocol.
constraints.uncertainty: The design co-evolution condition and referenced execution protocol are not supplied.

conditions: Design-profile completeness, promotion or closure is claimed.

grounding.quote:
- the final implementation is traceable to the accepted ontology;
- the final implementation is traceable to design and module boundary
  assets;
- unit tests are traceable to module ownership, not only to helper
  layout;
- implementation-first discoveries are reconciled into the ontology and
  the design's domain, sequence and state evidence before promotion or
  closure; and
- implementation may not compensate for an unrealised declared
  constructor by introducing a hidden controller or alternative authority
  path.

constraints.statement: Implementation must trace to accepted ontology, design and module assets; tests to module ownership. Reconcile implementation-first discoveries into ontology and domain/sequence/state evidence before promotion/closure; hidden controllers or alternative authority cannot compensate for unrealised constructors. Implementation-discovered tests must re-express closure proof against ownership; module boundaries enable common audit without outranking constitutional truth/ratified design. Minimum chain: constitutional WHAT; accepted ontology; target design; target module assets and ontology-derived carriers; accepted domain/sequence/state projections with axiom evaluation; implementation; tests from the same ontology/boundary. conditions: Unit tests are under the design profile.

proof; broader integration, scenario and sandbox lanes remain downstream
proof families; transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but they do not
replace module-derived unit proof. If a module has code but no
module-derived unit test lane, the module is not closure-ready under the
design profile. What such a lane claims, and what it never closes, is
the unit frame of §7.

constraints.statement: Tests should trace to accepted ontology and applicable entity/lifecycle/authority/function/effect/projection law, module design, active or equivalent carrier inventory, module-bounded domain/sequence/state projections and owned requirement families. Helper tests may exist but cannot be the canonical module proof. Broader integration/scenario/sandbox lanes remain downstream proof families, not substitutes. Transitional slice-gating does not replace the module lane; coded modules without it are not closure-ready. Design ownership does not extend to Product UAT/acceptance.

Each lifecycle phase takes one of the three answers that

owns, applied here to design evidence: answered by the active design,
requirement, release, deployment or telemetry surface; declared not

item, which in design evidence also names its owning follow-up. A phase
list without answers, not-applicable reasons or named gaps is not
design-method evidence (P5, P6). The three are declared states of the
design evidence for a phase under that section, not result values; a
named gap is a residual
([FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology)) that remains until its

and records them under `derivation_basis.principle_refs`. Each address

`a_c` does not choose the subject vocabulary, decide which source
declarations are material, supply semantic acceptance, select a carrier,
execute a model or prove that one interpretation is uniquely correct (P2,
P6).

constraints.statement: The calculus governs symbolic-model form: identities/types, exact relation endpoints, explicit constraints/latitude/residuals, typed traversals/judgments, closure/projection/overlay/transformation, subject preservation and separation of structural, semantic and authority claims. not (P2, P6).

Every `a_c` signature imports those identities unchanged. A model-family
signature specialises their fields, value domains, reference domains and
admissible kinds; it does not remove, rename, shadow or silently add a
core record family. Another fundamental record family requires an explicit

Every identity-bearing scalar/collection element is checked by RefDomain_Sigma: exact family, semantic sort where applicable, and exact external kind/basis; never both local and external. grounding.quote:
The following subsections define the exact shapes of five of the eight
core record families. `SemanticObject`, `TypedRelation`, `Constraint`,
`Latitude` and `Residual` populate `O`, `E`, `C`, `L` and `X`. The

record (AC-014) populate `V`, `T` and `J`. A traversal, transformation or
judgment is not placed in `O` merely by reifying its name as a semantic
object. A subject model may independently represent the concept of a
record kind, but that representation does not satisfy the core population
law (P3, P1).

grounding.quote:
`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves
one declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate
language and how its result is judged. A predicate that is not
deterministically decidable states the required probabilistic or human
judgment kind rather than pretending to be a machine proof (P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Declare the required probabilistic or human judgment kind instead of claiming machine proof. Both constraint and judgment kinds must resolve within the owning signature.

exceptions: Competent authority explicitly dispositions the residual.

grounding.quote:
Projection, compression, interpretation or encoding cannot erase a
residual. It remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent
authority, or causes refusal (P4b, P6).

`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines
its lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation
domains. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission
(P3).

constraints.statement: Projection, compression, interpretation and encoding cannot erase residuals: retain them, record competent disposition or refuse. Undeclared residual kinds or values refuse structural admission.

grounding.quote:
The objects these laws govern are the records of §2, §3 and §5 and the
ontology of FOUNDATIONS §2; where a law names identity, authority, basis
or residual, the definition is FOUNDATIONS' and the law is this member's.

constraints.statement: Fundamental laws govern records of sections 2, 3 and 5 and FOUNDATIONS §2 ontology. FOUNDATIONS retains definitions of identity, authority, basis and residual; this member owns the laws over them.

grounding.quote:
Every admitted object, relation, constraint, latitude, residual,
traversal, transformation specialisation and judgment belongs to one
declared signature. Every fundamental record also occurs exactly once in
the total `Population_M` function under its declared `RecordKind_ac`.
Missing, duplicate, shadowed or unknown record kinds and populations fail
closed (P3, P5).

constraints.statement: Every admitted fundamental record belongs to one declared signature and occurs exactly once under its declared core kind in total Population_M. Missing, duplicate, shadowed or unknown kinds/populations fail closed.

grounding.quote:

context, owner, scope and basis. That equal representations do not
establish equal meaning is FOUNDATIONS §2, Representation. The `a_c`
binding beside it: equal spelling, payload equality, position in any
structure and carrier equality do not establish semantic identity (P3).

constraints.statement: Every identity in I resolves one member under one type, context, owner, scope and basis. Owner maps to authority, type to kind, resolved member to denoted value; context/scope/basis are additional required coordinates permitted by IDENTITY §2. grounding.quote:
Every referenced identity resolves exactly once in the applicable model or
through one explicit external relation. Resolution uses the exact
`RefDomain_Sigma(source_record_kind, field)` declaration across the
model's record populations. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-record-kind,
wrong-sort, wrong-basis, locally-and-externally ambiguous or
undeclared-field references refuse structural admission (P3, P5).

constraints.statement: Every reference resolves exactly once locally or through one explicit external relation using its exact RefDomain_Sigma declaration. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-kind, wrong-sort, wrong-basis, local/external ambiguous and undeclared-field references refuse structural admission; AC-007 separately determines the refusal's core value by cause.

exceptions: Direction is immaterial only when the relation kind explicitly declares symmetry.

grounding.quote:
A relation is lawful only when its kind admits the exact source and target
sorts and all required qualifiers are present. Direction is material
unless the relation kind explicitly declares symmetry (P4a, P3).

constraints.statement: Lawfulness requires exact admitted endpoint sorts and all required qualifiers; direction is material subject to explicit symmetry.

grounding.quote:
Objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals,
transformations, projections and judgments retain their declared semantic,
operation, evaluation and decision authority (the kinds of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)). What
creates no authority is listed there; in `a_c` its instances are copying,
interpreting, encoding, evaluating and transporting a record, none of
which transfers authority (P6, P4b).

constraints.statement: All listed records and projections retain declared semantic, operation, evaluation and decision authority. Copying, interpreting, encoding, evaluating or transporting transfers none.

exceptions: Mixed bases require an explicit owned composite-basis record.

Every result binds its exact basis under
[RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates), which
owns the exact-basis rule for results; what a basis is, including that
mixed bases need an explicit composite relation, is FOUNDATIONS §2,
Basis. This law binds the same rule to every fundamental record and model
of `a_c`: each binds an exact basis, the composite-basis relation of a
mixed basis is an explicitly owned record, and individually valid
coordinates do not create a coherent composite basis by proximity (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Every result, fundamental record and model binds an exact basis. Individually valid nearby coordinates do not constitute coherent composite basis. FOUNDATIONS defines Basis and RF-005 owns result exactness; AC-006 applies it to records/models.

conditions: A constraint judgment is performed.

grounding.quote:
A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

constraints.statement: For the predicate that the constraint holds for its governed subject on exact basis: holds→satisfied with established predicate; failed→falsified with named counterexample; undecidable admissible evidence→indeterminate naming deciding evidence; outside applies_to/context/scope requiring an undeclared relation→out_of_frame naming that relation and source-given owner; unsupported subject/basis→invalid_basis naming repair. No mapping raises standing or coerces failure, absence, indeterminacy, out-of-scope or invalid basis to satisfied. A judgment not performed has no closed result, is not indeterminate and enters conjunction as planned assessment without a result.

conditions: A closure, projection, structural admission, transformation application or interpretation is applied.

grounding.quote: | `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |

constraints.statement: For the predicate that the operation yields its declared result on exact basis: declared result→satisfied, establishing availability of a proposed model/successor only, not acceptance/admission; hold→indeterminate when required evidence/observation/disposition is not yet admitted, naming what decides; gap→invalid_basis when a needed member/reference/resolution/declaration remains unresolved by its declared relation; refusal(constraint)→falsified for a demonstrated law/signature violation by what is judged or any refusal not naming a basis condition; refusal(basis)→invalid_basis for basis conditions without a demonstrated violation by what is judged. A resolved-to-no-target local/external reference is dangling and refuses, distinct from open external resolution. Basis-only causes include inexact seeds/relations/edge semantics/basis/scope, nonfinite/nonunique fixed points, unestablished input identity/basis/admission or mixed bases without composite relation. Refusal names its condition, admits no record/model/carrier and silently drops nothing.

grounding.quote:
A basis mismatch inside a model or a record, a
relation's qualifier record included, is mixed bases with no
composite-basis relation (AC-006): a coordinate of the model or record
binds, or a reference in it resolves on, a basis that the governing basis
relation does not admit, as a wrong-basis reference of AC-003 does. It is
a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.

constraints.statement: Cause is part of refusal value. A demonstrated violation by the judged record/model/carrier/transformation/application makes refusal(constraint), even with a basis condition; report the latter alongside as a separate invalid_basis result naming repair and the unsupported evaluation predicate, not the operation-outcome predicate. Known failure/counterexample survives conjunction. A defect in an input used as basis is a basis condition for that operation. Basis mismatch—including qualifier or wrong-basis reference—is always a basis condition, never signature-constraint violation, even when the signature declares the basis relation. Thus AC-001 violation may falsify model admission while invalidating the basis of projection over that model. Unapplied operations have no outcome. A gap stop is a closed invalid_basis result, distinct from missing-result conjunction gaps. Signature/traversal-specific stops map under §5. Unestablished closure/projection is invalid_basis for its predicate, as closure_unresolved is for its own activation predicate.

or transformation relation. An implementation preference, a probabilistic

the same rule for any two values; this law is its form over `L` and `T`

boundary or unproven relation remains in `X` until an authorised

and scope are exact and the fixed point is finite and unique. Failure to
establish those conditions returns a gap or refusal: `gap` where a

closure means least lawful record closure under `R`; it does not claim
globally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.
ACTIVATION §2 applies this closure to the construction of a step's context
under an envelope.

that no reference trims a required member to fit a carrier or budget,

body, applies to it: here the required members are those of the material

disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation or translation exists only as
